account:
Today has been mostly routine mayoral business, but there are unresolved rumours about bridge or port changes affecting bakery deliveries. I heard townspeople repeating those claims this morning, without any specific confirmed change. I went to the mill for the scheduled grain inspection but did not locate the miller or baker. The baker later visited my office on bakery business, offered bread at one emerald a loaf, and asked whether delivery changes were confirmed. The baker said freight delivered wheat last night, the bread stall was well stocked, and there was no confirmed grain shortage. The secretary has received no confirmation of access changes, and the neighbour has not seen the miller today either. I do not know why the miller was absent; that alone does not establish a supply problem. The rumours appear to be circulating among people concerned about deliveries, but I have no evidence of their source or any hidden purpose.

I attended lunch at home, the council-letters office session, and tea at the neighbour's cottage. No new correspondence has arrived, according to the secretary. I am now back at the office after tea. The builder is here holding a lantern and says they are ready to accompany me to the eighteen-hundred great-hall lighting inspection, which I confirmed yesterday. That looks consistent with the scheduled review of hall lighting. I have asked about dark spots, proposed remedies and costs, but have not yet received a substantive answer. The inspection remains ahead, followed by going home at nineteen hundred.
